description: NASA's NeoWs feed (JPL data) of near-Earth asteroids making their closest approach in the coming seven days: miss distance in lunar distances, estimated size and speed, and which are potentially hazardous (hover a dot for its record, click for its JPL page). Statistics: sizes span two orders of magnitude, so they are binned on a log scale, where the median and the geometric mean (the mean of the logs) describe a typical asteroid and the ordinary mean is pulled up by the few big ones. Sizes are modelled from brightness with an assumed albedo (min to max is a factor of about 2.2), small asteroids are only found when they pass close, and a week is a few dozen objects. Uses NASA's shared DEMO_KEY (30 requests an hour); put your own key in for more.
name: Asteroids passing Earth this week
